title: The Roman World
note: Rome's books, in reading order: the Rhetorica, then the Essentials' Rome module. Each stands in a zone of the city (content/rome/republican_rome.json) and belongs to one of the city's ages (content/rome/city.json): the city you walk is the age of the latest book you have mastered.

modules.title: The Speaker in the Forum
modules.intro: The Roman art of the speech, as it was taught in the last generation of the Republic: the five canons, the parts of a speech, the three styles, and the memory palace.
takeaways: Rhetoric has five parts: invention, arrangement, style, memory, and delivery.
A trained memory is a house of places walked in order, with a striking image set in each.

modules.title: Rome: Duty, Empire, and the Stoics
modules.intro: Rome took Greek culture and turned it toward law, duty, and empire, and it produced the Stoic writers still read as practical guides. This module gives you the founding myths, the national epic, and Stoicism in its own words.
takeaways: Roman virtue is duty to family, gods, and the state (pietas). Aeneas is its model, and Virgil shows what it costs.
The Stoics separate what is in our power (judgments, choices) from what is not (everything else).
The Epicureans (Lucretius) offer the rival cure: an atomic universe with no gods to fear and no death to suffer.

works.title: Rhetorica ad Herennium
works.read: Book I.2-4 (the five canons and the parts of a speech) and Book III.16-24 (the art of memory).

works.author: Livy
works.title: The History of Rome
works.read: The Preface and I.1-16 (the founding); I.57-60 (Lucretia and the end of the kings).
works.edition: Tr. Aubrey de Selincourt, The Early History of Rome and The War with Hannibal (Penguin)

works.author: Plutarch
works.title: Parallel Lives
works.edition: Tr. Robin Waterfield, Roman Lives and Greek Lives (Oxford World's Classics)

works.author: Virgil
works.title: The Aeneid
works.edition: Tr. Robert Fitzgerald (Vintage) or Robert Fagles (Penguin)

works.author: Lucretius
works.title: On the Nature of Things
works.read: I.1-158 (the invocation and 'nothing from nothing') and III.830-1094 ('death is nothing to us').
works.edition: Tr. Martin Ferguson Smith (Hackett); or A.E. Stallings (Penguin)

works.author: Cicero
works.title: On Duties
works.read: On Duties I.1-60 and On Friendship.
works.edition: On Duties tr. Griffin and Atkins (Cambridge Texts in the History of Political Thought); On Friendship and On Old Age in Cicero: On the Good Life, tr. Michael Grant (Penguin)

works.author: Cicero
works.title: The Dream of Scipio
works.read: The whole text; it is a few pages.
works.edition: In Cicero: The Republic and The Laws, tr. Niall Rudd (Oxford World's Classics)

works.author: Ovid
works.title: Metamorphoses
works.read: Book I (creation, the flood, Apollo and Daphne) and Book X (Orpheus, Pygmalion).
works.edition: Tr. Allen Mandelbaum (Harcourt) or Charles Martin (Norton)

works.author: Tacitus
